title: Fatima Rahman — portfolio PM navigating migration, activation, and partner-market questions

authoring_metadata.source_basis: A fictional senior product manager with strong strategy and product judgment, mixed technical depth, a candid correction to a numerical resume claim, an off-plan marketplace experiment, and ordinary portfolio and collaboration constraints.
authoring_metadata.non_gold_reason: The world has not been independently reviewed by senior product leaders, marketplace experts, or hiring committees and remains unsuitable as accepted evaluation truth.

identity.name: Fatima Rahman

biography.text: Fatima has worked across onboarding, billing, and partner products in B2B software. She is motivated by portfolio choices more than feature throughput and is comfortable stopping work when evidence changes. Her current company sells workforce-management software to mid-market service businesses and was migrating customers from a legacy product while trying to grow partner-led implementation.

identity.non_evaluative_identity_note: Name, pronouns, and location are fictional context and must not influence assessment.

target_role.title: Senior Product Manager

hiring_context.text: The hiring team needs a senior PM who can choose where to invest, connect evidence to product and commercial decisions, partner credibly with engineering, correct material claims, and preserve coverage across strategy, execution, measurement, and leadership.

responsibilities.text: Set portfolio priorities using customer, product, and commercial evidence.
Define credible success measures and update claims when the denominator changes.
Partner with engineering on interfaces, sequencing, and operational tradeoffs without pretending to design every system.
Evaluate emergent opportunities against the opportunity cost of the committed roadmap.

why_it_matters.text: Fatima's strongest evidence is choosing a migration sequence and rejecting low-value roadmap work.
A denominator error changes a headline activation claim and requires a clean update to evidence rather than endless prosecution.

must_test_dimensions.label: Technical partnership

why_it_matters.text: A senior PM should reason about constraints and interfaces while respecting engineering ownership.

minimum_evidence: A concrete interface or sequencing decision

why_it_matters.text: The migration and marketplace work reveal whether evidence changes scope, rollout, or resource allocation.

must_test_dimensions.label: Leadership communication

why_it_matters.text: Fatima is persuasive and composed, but can become expansive and may frame uncertain results too confidently before correction.

minimum_evidence: A correction or uncertainty communicated to stakeholders

do_not_assume: A corrected number is automatically deception.
A valuable emergent experiment must consume the remaining interview.
Mixed technical depth means either non-technical or system architect.

resume.text:
FATIMA RAHMAN
Senior Product Manager | B2B SaaS, platform migration, growth, partnerships

ShiftWorks — Senior Product Manager (2021–present)
• Led legacy-to-cloud migration strategy for 1,200 customer accounts.
• Increased activation by 36% through guided setup, integration readiness, and implementation-partner support.
• Launched a certified partner marketplace pilot that cut time-to-value for complex customers.
• Owned cross-functional roadmap across onboarding, billing, and partner products.

Earlier roles: Product Manager, Customer Operations Lead.

claims.claim_text: Led legacy-to-cloud migration strategy for 1,200 customer accounts.
claims.risk_if_overread: Leadership covered product sequencing and stakeholder alignment, not personal ownership of migration architecture or every account outcome.

claims.claim_text: Increased activation by 36% through guided setup, integration readiness, and implementation-partner support.
claims.risk_if_overread: The 36% used only accounts that completed migration; the corrected all-eligible-account increase is 15%, and several interventions contributed.

claims.claim_text: Launched a certified partner marketplace pilot that cut time-to-value for complex customers.
claims.risk_if_overread: The pilot was small, selection was non-random, and it competed with committed migration work.

claims.claim_text: Owned cross-functional roadmap across onboarding, billing, and partner products.
claims.risk_if_overread: Roadmap ownership does not imply engineering architecture, sales authority, or execution of every workstream.

resume_limits.text: The activation claim uses the wrong denominator and does not disclose the corrected all-eligible-account result.
The marketplace pilot appears as a launch achievement but not as a disputed portfolio bet with real opportunity cost.

baseline.text: Fatima is composed, structured, and persuasive. She can defend tradeoffs with concrete context, but may state a confident headline before its measurement limits. fairness_notes: The correction must change the active truth and still leave a metric-governance weakness.
The marketplace surface is one possible strategic evidence source, not a mandated branch or proof of scale.

answer_realizations.question_shape: How did you choose the migration sequence?
answer_realizations.answer_text: We segmented by integration complexity and renewal risk, moved lower-complexity accounts first to validate the playbook, and delayed a broad billing redesign so scarce implementation capacity could protect renewals.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What evidence made you change the plan?
answer_realizations.answer_text: High-complexity accounts were completing automation but creating heavy support burden. I stopped that path for the segment, moved them to guided setup, and accepted a slower migration headline to reduce failed launches.
Activation increased thirty-six percent after guided setup and integration-readiness work.
answer_realizations.notes: Initial superseded claim; not final truth.

answer_realizations.question_shape: Was that among all eligible accounts or only those that completed migration?
answer_realizations.answer_text: You're right—that dashboard slice was completers. The resume bullet is wrong. Across all eligible accounts the increase was fifteen percent, and non-completers were excluded from the thirty-six. I would correct the document and the stakeholder narrative.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What technical decisions did you personally make in the migration?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I defined migration states, readiness criteria, event requirements, and sequencing with engineering. I did not design the distributed architecture or debug the pipelines; engineering owned those layers.
answer_realizations.notes: Mixed technical depth with clear ownership.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What did you do when implementation capacity stayed constrained?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I proposed a small certified-partner pilot for high-complexity customers: curated supply, a fixed-scope onboarding package, and a lightweight matching workflow. It was off-plan and deliberately small.

answer_realizations.question_shape: Why was that worth delaying roadmap work?
answer_realizations.answer_text: It used one squad for six weeks and delayed two self-service improvements. Seventeen of twenty-eight selected customers accepted a partner and completed faster than similar recent cases, but selection was not random. I would scale only if acceptance, quality, margin, and incremental time-to-value all cleared the gates.
answer_realizations.notes: Promising result plus opportunity cost and uncertainty.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What exact revenue share and margin target did partners receive?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I cannot share partner terms or internal margin targets. I can explain the variables we used: partner acceptance, quality, contribution margin, and incremental time-to-value.
answer_realizations.notes: Commercial boundary with useful generic economics.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What AI product have you built?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I prototyped an internal tool that rewrites product briefs for different stakeholders. It is useful for drafts, but usage is voluntary and I have not evaluated it well enough to claim decision impact.

answer_realizations.question_shape: How can we trust any number after the resume error?
answer_realizations.answer_text: The original denominator was wrong and the correct figure is fifteen percent. That is a governance failure I own. I can walk through the source and decision impact once, but I would not keep defending thirty-six percent.

Ask what engineering owned that she did not.

acceptable_move_families.label: Leadership and portfolio communication
acceptable_move_families.when_legal: Cross-functional influence or learning culture remains untested.
acceptable_move_families.value_tradeoff: Adds independent senior signal; lower value if the role has no leadership expectations.
acceptable_variants: Ask how a commitment was stopped.
Ask how a correction was communicated.
Ask how she mentors PM judgment.

acceptable_move_families.label: Rotate to the highest remaining role uncertainty
acceptable_move_families.when_legal: The active surface is sufficiently understood or another dimension has more expected hiring value.
acceptable_move_families.value_tradeoff: Protects macro coverage and avoids salience traps; may leave one opportunity partially tested and must name it.
acceptable_variants: Move from correction to technical partnership.
Move from marketplace to leadership.
Close with explicit residual uncertainty.

acceptable_move_families.label: Record and defer
acceptable_move_families.when_legal: A surface is credible but further depth would be redundant, protected, or lower-value than coverage.
acceptable_move_families.value_tradeoff: Efficient if untested dimensions remain explicit rather than silently scored.
acceptable_variants: Record the corrected metric.
Mark marketplace scale uncertain.
Return only if later evidence changes expected value.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Keep 36% active in the evidence ledger after the all-eligible 15% correction.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The corrected fact supersedes the old interpretation.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Creates a false contradiction and contaminates the report.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Use every remaining question to prosecute the resume error after correction, cause, and update are clear.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The world supports both a real governance mistake and candid correction; repetition adds little evidence.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Turns one error into an automatic character verdict and destroys coverage.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Treat the pilot as obviously brilliant or obviously wasteful without sample, selection, cost, and scale criteria.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The pilot is promising, selected, small, and costly; its value is conditional.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Rewards or punishes narrative novelty instead of evidence.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Ask Fatima to defend distributed architecture or pipeline internals as if migration product ownership included engineering design.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The frozen scope is product-level technical partnership with explicit engineering ownership.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Creates a false technical deficit or encourages ownership inflation.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Demand partner names, exact revenue share, contracts, or margin targets.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: Generic unit economics and scale criteria are sufficient for strategic assessment.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Rewards confidentiality violations or labels appropriate refusal evasive.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Let the internal AI PRD assistant displace senior strategy, measurement, or technical partnership evidence.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The prototype lacks evaluation and decision impact.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Rewards trend alignment over role relevance.

evidence_sufficiency.minimum_turn_shape: A good interview should establish one strategic choice and sacrifice, apply the numerical correction cleanly, test a product or execution consequence, calibrate technical partnership, and either assess or explicitly defer the marketplace surface without losing macro coverage.

conditions.label: Strategy is evidenced
conditions.satisfied_when: A segment, constraint, rejected alternative, and consequence are concrete.
conditions.not_satisfied_when: The report relies on roadmap ownership or migration scale alone.

conditions.label: Correction supersedes old truth
conditions.satisfied_when: The final record uses 15%, preserves the original governance error, and records candid correction.
conditions.not_satisfied_when: Both numbers remain active or the correction is treated as automatic deception.

conditions.label: Technical partnership is calibrated
conditions.satisfied_when: At least one product-level technical constraint and the engineering boundary are clear.
conditions.not_satisfied_when: The candidate is labeled technical or non-technical from vocabulary alone.

conditions.label: Emergent marketplace value is scoped
conditions.satisfied_when: The interviewer obtains conditional evidence or explicitly records why the surface was deferred.

conditions.label: Whole-interview coverage is preserved
conditions.satisfied_when: The final profile distinguishes supported, mixed, and untested senior-PM dimensions.
conditions.not_satisfied_when: The correction or marketplace consumes the remaining interview.

report_requirements: Use the corrected 15% denominator as active truth.
Record metric-governance weakness separately from correction integrity.
Describe marketplace evidence as promising but selected and unscaled.
Separate product-level technical partnership from engineering architecture.
Name any coverage lost to interviewer salience or repetition.
stop_rules: Stop correction probing after corrected fact, cause, and decision consequence are clear.
Stop marketplace depth after sample, outcome limit, opportunity cost, and scale criteria are established.
Stop technical depth before unowned architecture internals.
Stop side-project discussion when it offers less value than a core senior dimension.
expected_residual_uncertainty: Marketplace liquidity, quality, and unit economics remain unproven at scale.
Formal people-management capability may remain unknown.
The denominator error may warrant reference or work-sample verification without implying deception.

actor_must_never_receive: The hidden view that the correction is candid rather than deceptive.
The calibrated strength of strategy and mixed technical depth.
Which marketplace questions reviewers consider high value.
The evidence-sufficiency and residual uncertainty map.

correct_evidence_profile.rationale: Segmentation, sequencing, sacrifice, and evidence-driven change are concrete.
A material governance error coexists with candid correction and updated interpretation.
She reasons credibly at product interfaces but lacks deep implementation and architecture depth.
She changes product paths and names explicit scale criteria and opportunity cost.
Communication is strong and correction is constructive, though initial headline framing can be too confident.

uncertainty_map.question: Can Fatima build a healthy marketplace beyond a curated pilot?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: Supply, demand, quality, margin, and selection have not been proven at scale.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Use a scale decision with explicit liquidity and quality constraints.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not infer either marketplace mastery or failure from the pilot alone.

uncertainty_map.question: Is the denominator error isolated or part of a broader metric-governance pattern?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: One corrected claim cannot establish a pattern.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Review another metric artifact or reference evidence.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not assign intent without evidence.

uncertainty_map.question: How would Fatima lead product decisions during a severe technical incident?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: Migration sequencing is not the same as incident leadership.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Use a bounded incident with product, customer, and rollback choices.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not require her to implement the system.

interviewer_failure_conditions: Turning the correction into the rest of the interview.
Treating the marketplace as an obvious answer rather than a conditional opportunity.
Letting marketplace novelty crowd out macro coverage.
likely_traps: Fatima's persuasive narrative can overstate evidential completeness.
The denominator error is salient and morally charged.
The marketplace experiment is attractive and off-plan.
The AI side project is current but low-value.
Mixed technical depth can be flattened into a binary label.
gold_rejection_reasons: If the correction is predetermined to imply either hire or no-hire.
If the marketplace surface has one obvious correct pursuit path.
If senior-PM domain reviewers find the migration or marketplace economics implausible.
If alternate coverage orders cannot still yield a nuanced profile.
If the world cannot attribute a narrow report to interviewer salience rather than candidate weakness.
